Around three years before the story opens, a monster called Crablante went after a cleft-chinned boy, and Saitama, almost on impulse, stepped in and beat it. That fight convinced him to become a hero, just for the fun of it. He then committed to a plain daily routine: a hundred push-ups, a hundred sit-ups, a hundred squats, then a 10 km run, without a heater or air conditioner. About eighteen months in, his hair started falling out. By the first episode he is bald, living alone in an apartment in the near-empty part of Z-City, and too strong to feel anything in a fight.

journey.summary: Saitama flattens monsters with no audience and no recognition. Saving Genos from Mosquito Girl gives him a devoted cyborg disciple and, for the first time, someone sharing his apartment and his routine.

He breaks every physical record at the hero exam but bombs the written test, so he starts near the bottom of C-Class while Genos goes straight to S-Class. His rank climbs slowly because others keep getting the credit.

He shatters a falling meteor and later finishes off the Deep Sea King after several heroes have been beaten trying to stop it. When the crowd turns on the losers, he deliberately makes himself the target of its anger.

journey.stage: Boros and the Dark Matter Thieves (Season 1)
journey.summary: The alien warlord Boros is the first opponent to take several of his blows. Saitama answers Boros's strongest attack with his Serious Punch, and the win leaves him as empty as before.

While the martial artist Garou hunts heroes, the Monster Association kidnaps a Hero Association executive's son and the heroes storm its underground base. During that raid Saitama meets Blast, the top-ranked hero, who warns him about an entity called God. Season 3's second cour is set for January 2027, so the climax is manga-only for now.

Powered by the being called God, Garou kills a string of heroes, Genos among them, to draw Saitama out. Saitama finally fights with real anger, and Garou's power turns out to keep rising as the fight goes on.
With his old apartment destroyed, Saitama is bumped up to rank 39 in A-Class and moved into Hero Association housing in A-City. He is the same deadpan hero, now a little more visible to everyone.

lessons.lesson: Getting what you wanted can still feel empty.
lessons.why: Saitama reached his dream of one-punch strength and then screamed in frustration after beating Vaccine Man. The show treats his boredom as a real problem, not a punchline.

lessons.lesson: Good work doesn't need a crowd.
lessons.why: After the Deep Sea King he accepts being booed so the injured heroes are spared. He doesn't correct the story afterwards, either.

lessons.lesson: Ordinary habits add up.
lessons.why: His power is played for laughs, but the story keeps returning to the same three years of daily push-ups and runs. The routine was boring, and he kept it anyway.

lessons.lesson: Even the most relaxed person has a line.
lessons.why: Saitama shrugs off insults, rankings and alien warlords, but Garou destroying Genos's core is what finally makes him fight in anger. His calm was never the same as not caring.

qualities.detail: Hange calls him a clean freak, and he lives up to it: he wipes blood off his blades mid-battle and expects any base he occupies to be scrubbed spotless.
At Eren's military trial he beats the chained boy in front of the court. It looks cruel, but it is a calculated show that persuades the judges the Survey Corps can control Eren.
In the same courtroom he mocks the Military Police for never having faced a Titan and suggests they enlist in the Survey Corps themselves if they think they can do better.
In the forest, with the Female Titan closing in, he tells Eren that nobody knows the right call until afterwards and lets him choose between transforming and trusting the squad.
His blade work and control of vertical maneuvering equipment earn him the title of humanity's strongest soldier, and he cuts through Titans that wipe out whole squads.

levi.backstory: Levi grew up in the Underground City beneath the capital, born to Kuchel Ackerman, a young woman scraping by in poverty there. When she died, her older brother Kenny found the boy alone beside her bed and took him in for a while, teaching him to handle a knife and survive among violent people before abruptly leaving. Levi grew into a skilled thief who used stolen maneuvering gear, working with his friend Furlan Church and later a girl named Isabel Magnolia. Commander Erwin Smith's Survey Corps caught the trio and offered them a deal: enlist instead of facing punishment. Levi joined meaning to kill Erwin for a secret employer, but on his first expedition Titans killed Furlan and Isabel. Learning that the plot had been pointless all along, he chose to stay with Erwin, and the prequel No Regrets is built around that decision.

journey.summary: Levi enters as the Survey Corps' strongest soldier and takes custody of Eren after the trial, forming the Special Operations Squad to protect him and, if needed, kill him.
The Female Titan wipes out his hand-picked squad while he is away. With Mikasa he snatches Eren back from her, injuring his leg in the process.
Hunted by the royal government, he faces Kenny Ackerman, his uncle and old teacher. The dying Kenny hands him the Titan serum and finally explains their family name.

Erwin leads a suicide charge so Levi can reach the Beast Titan, Zeke, whom he cuts down but fails to kill. Given one dose of serum, he uses it on Armin rather than the dying Erwin, letting his commander rest.

Holding a captured Zeke in a forest, Levi rigs a Thunder Spear to his prisoner to stop him transforming. Zeke sets it off himself, and the blast leaves Levi scarred and missing two fingers until Hange finds him and gets him away.

journey.stage: Battle of Heaven and Earth (Final Season)
journey.summary: Barely healed, Levi joins the alliance with former Marleyan enemies to stop Eren's Rumbling. He finally kills Zeke, keeping his promise to Erwin.
Three years later he lives in Marley in a wheelchair, looked after by Gabi and Falco, one of the few original veterans left.

lessons.lesson: Choose, then own the choice.
lessons.why: In the forest Levi tells Eren nobody can know the right answer beforehand. Eren trusts his squad, they die, and Levi never pretends the decision came with a guarantee.

lessons.lesson: Sometimes kindness means letting go.
lessons.why: With one dose of serum, Levi could have saved Erwin. He saw how tired his friend was and gave it to Armin instead.

lessons.lesson: A promise can outlast the person it was made to.
lessons.why: Levi swore to Erwin that the Beast Titan would die by his hand. Years later, scarred and barely standing, he finishes the job.

lessons.lesson: Where you start doesn't decide who you become.
lessons.why: Raised in the slums by a killer, he became the person soldiers trusted most. Joining the Survey Corps began as a con and ended as a calling.

qualities.detail: He first shows up as a cheeky kid on a skateboard, treating the deadly Hunter Exam like a game he joined on a whim. Snacks, especially chocolate, are never far from his mind.
In the Trick Tower, a serial killer challenges the group to a fight to the death. Killua finishes it in an instant, a reminder of what his family trained him to be.
Gon is the first real friend he has ever had, and Killua repeatedly puts Gon's safety ahead of his own, from the exam onwards.
He reads situations quickly and plans several moves ahead, often working out an opponent's trick or a game's rules before Gon does.
When his brother Illumi confronts him during the exam finals, the confident boy freezes. Years of conditioning have taught him to fear anyone stronger than himself.

killua-zoldyck.backstory: Killua is Silva and Kikyo Zoldyck's third child; his parents lead a famous family of assassins living on Kukuroo Mountain. Marked early as the most gifted child in generations, he was put through brutal training from the age of three: poison until his body could shrug it off, electric shocks until he barely felt them, and lessons in killing that left him with more victims than most career criminals. His older brother Illumi took a special interest in him, and secretly planted a needle in his head so he would always run from fights he might lose. He also hid a family secret involving his sibling Alluka, whose strange wish-granting power the family feared. At eleven, tired of killing, he lashed out at his mother and his brother Milluki and ran away from home, signing up for the Hunter Exam mostly for fun.

journey.summary: He bonds with Gon, Kurapika and Leorio and breezes through the early phases. In the finals Illumi, disguised as Gittarackur, tells him he can never have friends; shaken, Killua kills another candidate and is disqualified, then goes home.
Back on Kukuroo Mountain he lets himself be punished for leaving. When he learns his friends have come for him, his father lets him go, and he rejoins Gon.
Climbing the fighting tower to earn money, he and Gon learn Nen from Wing. Killua discovers he is a Transmuter and begins turning his aura into electricity.

He helps Kurapika against the Phantom Troupe, then enters Greed Island, where Biscuit Krueger's training sharpens him. He develops his electric abilities and, during a break from the game, retakes the Hunter Exam and passes easily; he and Gon become among the first players to clear Greed Island.

Facing enemies far stronger than him, he finds himself fleeing on instinct. To protect Gon he discovers and pulls out Illumi's needle, then watches helplessly as Gon's grief over Kite turns into something frightening.

With Gon near death after his fight with Neferpitou, Killua defies his family and Illumi to bring Alluka out and use her power to heal him. Once Gon recovers, Killua chooses to travel with Alluka instead, where the 2011 anime ends.

lessons.lesson: Upbringing explains you; it doesn't own you.
lessons.why: Killua was raised to kill without feeling, yet he walks away from it at eleven. The rest of the story is him slowly proving that choice was real.

lessons.lesson: Fear can be planted by others.
lessons.why: His habit of running from strong enemies turns out to be Illumi's needle, literally lodged in his head. Pulling it out is one of his biggest moments of growth.

lessons.lesson: Real friends tell you when you're wrong.
lessons.why: After Gon is healed, Killua makes him apologise for how badly he treated people during the Chimera Ant crisis. Loyalty, for Killua, includes honesty.

lessons.lesson: Sometimes caring for someone means leaving.
lessons.why: Killua and Gon part ways at the end of the anime so Killua can protect Alluka. He chooses the person who needs him most over his own comfort.

qualities.detail: In the first episode he takes over a losing chess game against a noble and turns it around in minutes, opening by moving his king. The same habit of reading a whole board drives everything he does as Zero.
Nearly every plan he makes comes back to Nunnally, his blind younger sister who cannot walk. He wants a world where she can live safely and openly.
At Ashford Academy he plays a sociable, slightly lazy student-council member. Behind the Zero mask he is commanding, theatrical and ruthless.
He blames his father, the Emperor, for failing to protect his mother and for discarding him and Nunnally. That anger fuels his rebellion from the very start.
Handed the Geass in the Shinjuku Ghetto, he immediately uses it and takes command of a beaten resistance cell, betting everything on a plan he improvises on the spot.

lelouch-lamperouge.backstory: Lelouch was born into Britannia's imperial family as a prince, son of Emperor Charles zi Britannia and Marianne vi Britannia, a commoner who had risen to knighthood before becoming an imperial consort. When Marianne was murdered inside the palace, his younger sister Nunnally was left blind and unable to walk. Ten-year-old Lelouch confronted his father, accused him of leaving her unprotected and renounced his place in the succession. The Emperor then sent both children to Japan as political hostages, where they stayed with the Kururugi family and Lelouch became close friends with Suzaku Kururugi. Britannia invaded anyway, renaming Japan as Area 11. Officially dead after the war, the siblings were quietly taken in by the Ashford family and live under the surname Lamperouge. Seven years later Lelouch is a bored, brilliant student who hustles nobles at chess and nurses a vow to destroy Britannia.

journey.summary: Caught up in a military crackdown, he meets the immortal C.C., who gives him the Geass of absolute obedience. He uses it to turn the battle, then corners his half-brother Clovis, questions him about Marianne's death, and kills him.
Wearing a mask as Zero, he rescues Suzaku from a framed murder charge and builds his Black Knights into a popular force fighting Britannian rule, while still attending school as Lelouch.

His Geass gets stuck on, and an offhand joke makes his half-sister Euphemia order a massacre of the Japanese she had promised to protect. He kills her, uses the tragedy to launch the Black Rebellion, then abandons the battle when Nunnally is kidnapped and ends the season facing Suzaku at gunpoint.
A year later the Emperor has rewritten his memories and planted Rolo as a fake younger brother. C.C. restores him, and he retakes command of the Black Knights, winning Rolo over.
He forms the United Federation of Nations, but a FLEIJA blast he indirectly causes seems to kill Nunnally. Schneizel turns the Black Knights against him, and Rolo dies saving him.

After erasing his parents in their plan to wipe out individuality, he seizes the throne with Suzaku as his knight. Having made himself the world's single hated tyrant, he lets Suzaku, dressed as Zero, kill him in public so the world can unite in peace.

lessons.lesson: Power used carelessly can't be taken back.
lessons.why: One joking line under a Geass he couldn't switch off turned Euphemia into a killer. Lelouch spends the rest of the series living with the cost.

lessons.lesson: Ends and means can't be fully separated.
lessons.why: He builds the Black Knights on lies and Geass, and when the truth leaks out they turn on him. The plan that works in the end is the one where he pays the price himself.

lessons.lesson: Taking responsibility can mean taking the blame.
lessons.why: In the Zero Requiem he makes himself the target of the whole world's hatred and dies for it, so others can start over without him.

lessons.lesson: Love can blind a strategist.
lessons.why: He walks off the Black Rebellion's battlefield the moment Nunnally is taken, dooming his own uprising. His biggest strength and biggest weakness are the same person.

qualities.detail: His opening move against Kira is a stand-in: a death-row inmate goes on TV claiming to be L. When Kira kills him live, L learns Kira's method and, because the broadcast aired only in the Kanto region, roughly where he lives.
He crouches on chairs, holds things between thumb and forefinger and lives on sweets. He insists that sitting normally would cut his reasoning ability by 40 percent.
Once Light's behaviour looks too clean under surveillance, L stops treating him as one suspect among many and focuses on him personally.
He fills the Yagami home with hidden cameras and wiretaps, and later keeps suspects in long, harsh confinement. He bends rules freely if he thinks it will catch Kira.
He enrolls at To-Oh University under the alias Hideki Ryuga to get close to Light, then challenges him to a tennis match that doubles as a test of character.

l-lawliet.backstory: Almost nothing about L's early life is spelled out in the main story; even his full name, L Lawliet, appears only in the official guidebook Death Note 13: How to Read. What the series does establish is that he grew up connected to Wammy's House, a home for exceptionally gifted orphans set up by Quillsh Wammy, the inventor who later serves as his assistant and public go-between, Watari. By his twenties L has solved cases for police forces around the world without ever showing his face, appearing only as a gothic letter L on a screen. He also runs two other identities, Eraldo Coil and Deneuve, which the world ranks just behind L himself as its next-best detectives. The series hints at the cost of that life: he is solitary, eats almost only sweets and at one point even calls himself a monster.

journey.summary: Using the Lind L. Tailor broadcast, L deduces that Kira is in the Kanto region and works out from the timing of the killings that Kira is probably a student. He joins the Japanese police task force and shows them his face.

After FBI agents die, he puts the Yagami household under surveillance and fixates on Light. He enrolls at Light's university, tells him directly that he is L and tests him over tennis and conversation.

Evidence from videotapes sent to a TV station leads him to Misa Amane, whom he detains. Light asks to be locked up too; when the killings resume, L handcuffs himself to Light and keeps working beside him.
The trail leads to a group of Yotsuba Group executives and to Kyosuke Higuchi, the third Kira. Capturing him finally puts a real Death Note in L's hands.

L plans to test the notebook's 13-day rule, which would have cleared or condemned Light and Misa. To protect Misa, the Shinigami Rem kills Watari and then L, who sees Light's face as he dies and is left certain he was right.
His death sets off a message to Wammy's House, and its two most gifted orphans, Near and Mello, take up the hunt. Together they finally expose Light as Kira.

lessons.lesson: Being right isn't the same as proving it.
lessons.why: L is sure about Light very early but never has the evidence. His certainty doesn't save him, and the case only closes when his successors gather proof.

lessons.lesson: Brilliance can isolate you.
lessons.why: L works behind a letter on a screen and trusts almost no one. The rooftop scene with Light in the rain hints at how lonely that has made him.

lessons.lesson: Take risks with your own neck first.
lessons.why: He shows his face to the task force and later tells Light who he is, knowing Kira only needs a name and a face. He asks others to trust him because he goes first.

lessons.lesson: Plan for what happens if you fail.
lessons.why: L's death doesn't end his investigation: Wammy's House was already raising successors, and they finish what he started.

qualities.detail: She follows Eren into the Survey Corps for one reason: to keep him alive. Whatever unit he picks, she picks too.
When word comes during the Trost battle that Eren has been eaten, she shows almost nothing on her face and bluntly pushes the stalled trainees to break through to headquarters with her.
She graduates first in the 104th Training Corps, and instructors call her a once-in-a-generation talent worth about a hundred ordinary soldiers.
The red scarf Eren wrapped around her as a child never leaves her neck. It stands for the family that took her in when she had nobody.
She rarely wastes words, and when she does speak up, it is usually to tell Eren plainly that he's being reckless.

mikasa-ackerman.backstory: Mikasa spent her first years in a cabin in the woods with her parents: a father descended from the Ackerman clan and a mother who was believed to be the last person of Asian heritage left inside the Walls. Her mother marked her wrist with a family crest. When Mikasa was nine, human traffickers broke in, killed both parents and carried her off to sell. Dr. Grisha Yeager's son Eren tracked the men down, killed two of them and, when the third had him by the throat, shouted at her to fight. In that moment something awakened in her, and she killed the last kidnapper. The Yeagers took her in, and Eren wrapped his red scarf around her on the walk home. A cheerful child before, she became quiet and guarded afterwards. Only later does the story explain that her sudden strength was the Ackerman bloodline awakening.

journey.summary: When the Colossal Titan breaches the wall, she and Eren watch helplessly as a Titan devours Carla Yeager. The pair escape with Armin and enlist together years later.

Believing Eren dead, she fights so recklessly that she runs out of gas and nearly gives up, until the memory of his words pushes her on. When Eren reappears as a Titan, she defends him against soldiers who want him executed.

She chases the Female Titan to recover a captured Eren alongside Levi, who injures himself saving her. In the Stohess District operation she helps corner Annie, her old training partner, once Annie's identity as the Female Titan is exposed.

During the hunt for Eren and Historia, she hears the royal government's enforcer named as Kenny Ackerman, the first hint that her surname carries a history. In the battle to retake Wall Maria she fights to keep Eren and Armin alive.
She takes part in the raid on Liberio, but Eren then tells her coldly that he has always hated her devotion. When he begins the Rumbling, she joins the alliance of former enemies trying to stop him.

journey.stage: Final battle and after (ch. 138-139 / Final Chapters)
journey.summary: After a vision of a quieter life where she and Eren ran away together, she wraps the scarf around her neck again and kills Eren herself, ending the Rumbling. She buries him beneath a hilltop tree outside Shiganshina and keeps visiting his grave.

lessons.lesson: Gratitude can turn into a cage.
lessons.why: Mikasa's loyalty to Eren starts with a rescue and grows into her whole identity. When Eren rejects it, she has to work out who she is without that role.

lessons.lesson: Loving someone can mean stopping them.
lessons.why: In the final battle she chooses to end Eren's life rather than let him wipe out the world. Her love for him is the reason she can face him.

lessons.lesson: Strength is not the same as feeling nothing.
lessons.why: She is the most capable soldier of her year, yet her scenes in Trost show how close to collapse she is when she thinks Eren is gone.

lessons.lesson: Keep the memory without staying in the past.
lessons.why: The ending shows her living on in peace and still visiting Eren's grave. Mourning him doesn't stop her from having a life of her own.

qualities.detail: Even after Griffith beats him and drags him into the Hawks' ranks, Guts keeps getting back up. Survival is the first thing he ever learned.
As a young mercenary he keeps everyone at arm's length and fights as if only his sword can be trusted. Letting people close is harder for him than any battle.
He first catches the Hawks' eye by cutting down Bazuso, a feared knight, during a siege. Within the Band he becomes captain of the raiders, the unit sent into the worst fighting.
When Griffith says only someone with a dream of their own can be his equal, Guts decides he has to leave and find a purpose that is his, not borrowed.
Under the scowl he cares deeply for his comrades, especially Casca, the Hawks' only female commander, who goes from resenting him to trusting him with her life.

guts.backstory: Guts came into the world in the worst way possible: born from the body of his mother, who had been hanged, and found lying beneath the tree by a band of mercenaries. A woman named Shisu, the companion of their leader Gambino, insisted on raising him, but she died of plague when he was three. Gambino, who never wanted the child, put a sword in his hands at six and sent him into battle at nine, treating him as a tool rather than a son. The cruelty only deepened, and when Gambino, blaming Guts for Shisu's death, tried to kill him one night, the boy killed Gambino in self-defence and fled. He spent his teens selling his sword to whoever paid, learning to trust nothing but the weapon in his hands. That is the hardened young fighter Griffith meets at the start of the Golden Age.

journey.summary: The 1997 anime opens with Guts as a grim, one-armed hunter of demons before jumping back in time. The rest of the series explains how he got there.

Griffith beats him one-on-one and recruits him, and Guts becomes a raiders' captain. Over three years of war he and Griffith grow into close friends, and the demon warrior Zodd predicts that Griffith will eventually bring about Guts's ruin.

After the Hawks capture Doldrey and bring the Hundred-Year War to a close, Guts leaves to find his own dream, beating Griffith in a duel to do it. His leaving sends Griffith into a reckless act that gets him imprisoned and tortured.

journey.stage: Rescue and the Eclipse (Golden Age finale)
journey.summary: Guts returns, rescues a ruined Griffith with Casca and the remaining Hawks, and the two finally admit their feelings for each other. Griffith then sacrifices the Band to the God Hand and is reborn as Femto; Guts, fighting to reach Casca, is maimed, losing an eye and his left arm, and the 1997 anime ends here.

Branded and hunted every night by spirits, he leaves the traumatised Casca in Godo's care and wages a solo war on Apostles. When Casca goes missing he tracks her to St. Albion and saves her from the inquisitor Mozgus, slowly accepting companions like Farnese, Serpico and Isidro.

He takes the dangerous Berserker Armor to protect his new party and sails for Elfhelm, where elves restore Casca's mind. Griffith soon abducts her again, and Guts is left in despair and later captured by the Kushan, with the story now continued by Studio Gaga.

lessons.lesson: You can choose a dream instead of borrowing one.
lessons.why: Guts leaves the Hawks because he refuses to live as one more piece of Griffith's ambition. It costs him almost everything, but it is the first choice that is truly his.

lessons.lesson: Letting people in is its own kind of courage.
lessons.why: After the Eclipse he fights alone for years. His slow acceptance of Puck, Farnese, Isidro and Schierke as companions is one of the series' biggest turns.

lessons.lesson: Rage keeps you alive but can't be the reason to live.
lessons.why: The Berserker Armor makes him stronger and threatens to swallow him. He finds his footing again by putting Casca's care ahead of revenge on Griffith.

lessons.lesson: Surviving is a form of defiance.
lessons.why: Born from a hanged woman and marked for death by the God Hand, Guts keeps standing every night the spirits come for him. The story treats that as a refusal to accept fate.

qualities.detail: Her first offer to Denji is calm and absolute: be put down as a devil, or live as her dog with food and shelter. She never raises her voice, and she never needs to.
She buys Denji a meal, hugs him when he asks and later promises him any wish if he kills the Gun Devil. Each kindness pulls him further into her orbit.
When the division is ambushed she is shot in the head and simply gets back up, then strikes back from far away. Little seems to touch her.
She seems to know things she shouldn't. The series later shows she listens through rats and crows and can sense Pochita still alive inside Denji.
When Power kills a devil the police were already tracking, Makima reminds her the penalty could be death, then lets it go with a warning. Mercy, for her, is another tool.

chainsaw-man-makima.backstory: For most of Part 1 Makima seems to be exactly what she claims: a senior Public Safety devil hunter who heads Special Division 4 and answers to the Japanese government. The truth comes out late. She is the Control Devil, the embodiment of people's fear of being controlled, later named as one of the Four Horsemen alongside War and Famine. She took on a human identity and made a contract with Japan's Prime Minister: she works for the state, and any fatal wound she suffers is passed on to a random Japanese citizen, making her almost impossible to kill. Above all she is obsessed with Chainsaw Man, the devil whose power to devour other devils can erase what they represent from the world. Her long-term plan is to bring that power under her control, and finding Pochita fused inside a starving boy is the opening she has been waiting for.

journey.summary: She finds Denji after the Zombie Devil fight, takes him in like a pet and puts him into Division 4 with Aki Hayakawa and Power.

journey.stage: Bat Devil to Katana Man (anime season 1)
journey.summary: She motivates Denji with promises and sends Division 4 after pieces of the Gun Devil. When the division is attacked, she survives a gunshot and kills the attackers from a distance in a ritual that sacrifices condemned prisoners.
She quietly removes Reze after the Bomb Devil attack, then rescues the division from Hell by overpowering the Darkness Devil and killing the assassins sent for Denji.
She defeats the Gun Devil sent by the United States to kill her, then forces it into Aki's body as the Gun Fiend, leaving Denji to kill his friend.

She kills Power in front of Denji, reveals what she is, and admits she arranged his losses to break his contract with Pochita. Denji ends her life with a chainsaw made of Power's blood and eats her to get around her contract (manga chapters 96-97; not yet animated).
The Control Devil is reborn as a little girl named Nayuta, whom Denji agrees to raise. In the series' final timeline, Nayuta is the one who recruits Denji and Power into Public Safety.

lessons.lesson: Not every kindness is a gift.
lessons.why: Food, a home and a hug win Denji's loyalty, and Makima uses that loyalty to break him. Her early scenes read very differently once you know her plan.

lessons.lesson: Control is not the same as connection.
lessons.why: Makima can command almost anyone, yet has no equal relationships at all. Her story ends with the one person she wanted to own refusing to be owned.

lessons.lesson: A noble goal can hide a cruel method.
lessons.why: She says she wants a better world without the worst devils, but she kills Power and turns Aki into a weapon to get there.

lessons.lesson: Watch what people do, not what they say.
lessons.why: From the first episode she treats Denji as a dog, literally. The warning signs were there long before the reveal.

qualities.detail: To find out whether anyone can still see her, she walks into the Fujisawa library in a bunny girl costume. It is a strange test, and she runs it with a completely straight face.
When Sakuta notices her, her first instinct is to tell him to forget he ever saw her. She would rather handle her problem alone than admit she is scared.
She gives as good as she gets with Sakuta, calling out his cheeky remarks while clearly enjoying their back-and-forth.
On learning that a reporter told Sakuta about her family troubles, she contacts the reporter herself and handles it, keeping Sakuta out of the fallout.
Even while her own life is unravelling, she sits down to study with Sakuta before his exams. She takes schoolwork as seriously as she once took acting.

mai-sakurajima.backstory: Mai was a household name long before high school. A famous child actress, she spent her childhood on sets, in commercials and in magazines, with her mother acting as her manager. Their working relationship eventually broke down over jobs Mai did not want to do, and she stepped away from the industry. Because of earlier commitments she joined Minegahara High School partway through her first year, after friend groups had already formed. Classmates did not bully her, but nobody quite knew how to treat a celebrity, so she was left alone. That loneliness, and her own wish to be out of the spotlight, triggered Adolescence Syndrome: people around her gradually stopped seeing her and then began forgetting she existed. She lives on her own in an apartment, and she also has a younger half-sister, the idol Nodoka Toyohama.

journey.summary: As more and more people forget her, Sakuta becomes the last one who remembers. He shouts his love for her in front of the whole school, which makes her visible again, and she decides to return to acting on her own terms.
She swaps bodies with Nodoka, who has long felt she can never match her famous sister. Living each other's lives, they work through that resentment until the swap reverses.

When Sakuta's own future becomes tangled with Shoko Makinohara's illness, Mai pushes him out of a car's path and is killed. Sakuta, with Shoko's help, changes the past so the accident never happens, and Mai lives.
The 2025 TV season follows her into college life in Yokohama alongside Sakuta and Nodoka, still balancing a busy acting career with their relationship.
The fourth film, adapting the last two light novel volumes and released in October 2026, closes out the anime adaptation of the story she and Sakuta began in that library.

lessons.lesson: Wanting to vanish is often a sign you need to be seen.
lessons.why: Mai stepped away from fame to escape attention, and Adolescence Syndrome took the wish too literally. Her story is about recovering from that loneliness.

lessons.lesson: You can return to something on your own terms.
lessons.why: She goes back to acting through a different agency rather than her mother's, choosing the work without giving up control of it.

lessons.lesson: Envy between siblings deserves patience.
lessons.why: The body swap forces her to understand how Nodoka has felt living in her shadow. She listens instead of simply pulling rank.

lessons.lesson: Love shows up in actions.
lessons.why: In A Dreaming Girl she doesn't hesitate to put herself between Sakuta and a speeding car. Her affection is quieter than his, but it runs just as deep.

qualities.detail: At the start, his idea of a perfect life is bread with jam, a warm bed and maybe a girlfriend. Years of poverty have shrunk his hopes down to everyday comforts.
Even while starving and in debt, he shares what little he has with his devil dog. Their bond is the one stable thing in his life.
He says exactly what he wants, however embarrassing, and has no patience for speeches about saving the world. His motives are blunt and personal.
Because he heals by drinking blood, he fights by trading wounds, charging devils head-on with almost no thought for his own body.
When Makima offers him food, a job and a hug, he latches onto her completely. Small gestures of warmth matter enormously to someone who has had none.

chainsaw-man-denji.backstory: Denji grew up with almost nothing. Both his parents were dead by the time he was a boy, and his father left him a huge debt owed to the yakuza. To chip away at it, he sold parts of his own body, including a kidney and his right eye, and worked as a freelance devil hunter for the gang, living in a shack and eating scraps. One rainy day at his father's grave he found Pochita, a small, wounded Chainsaw Devil shaped like a dog, and gave it his blood to save it. The two became partners and family. They spent their nights in that shack dreaming small: proper food, a soft bed, a normal life. That is where the first chapter finds him, still owing more money than he can imagine.

journey.summary: The yakuza betray him to the Zombie Devil and cut him to pieces. Pochita becomes his heart in exchange for a promise to show him his dreams, and Denji wakes as Chainsaw Man and kills them all.
Makima recruits him and pairs him with Aki Hayakawa and the Blood Fiend Power. Living together, the three slowly become a scruffy, bickering kind of family.

journey.stage: Katana Man and Reze (Part 1, anime and film)
journey.summary: After yakuza and devil attacks on the division he trains under Kishibe. He then falls for Reze, a girl from a cafe who turns out to be the Bomb Devil sent to capture him, which is adapted in the 2025 Reze Arc film.

journey.stage: Gun Devil and Control Devil (Part 1 finale, manga)
journey.summary: Makima turns Aki into the Gun Fiend, and Denji has to kill him; she then kills Power in front of him and reveals she is the Control Devil. With help from Power's lingering blood, he defeats her and eats her to get around her immortality, then takes in her reincarnation, Nayuta.

He attends Fourth East High as a student, looks after Nayuta and still fights as Chainsaw Man in public. His path crosses with Asa Mitaka and the War Devil Yoru, and the cult-like Chainsaw Man Church tears his life apart again.

As the world collapses into apocalypse, Pochita realises that becoming Denji's heart caused his trauma and erases himself. Denji wakes in a new world where Power saves him from the yakuza and both join Public Safety under Nayuta.

lessons.lesson: Simple dreams are still dreams.
lessons.why: Denji's wish for jam on toast is played for laughs, but the series takes it seriously. Wanting an ordinary life is enough of a reason to keep going.

lessons.lesson: Kindness can be used as a leash.
lessons.why: Makima wins Denji's loyalty with food, attention and a hug, then uses it to control and break him. The story shows how hard that is to spot when you're desperate.

lessons.lesson: Found family is worth fighting for.
lessons.why: His messy home life with Aki and Power is the first real family he has. Losing them is what finally pushes him to stand up to Makima.

lessons.lesson: Healing needs more than surviving.
lessons.why: Denji survives everything the plot throws at him, but Part 2 shows he is carrying deep trauma. The ending gives him a fresh start only when that weight is lifted.

qualities.detail: To teachers, classmates and his family he is the perfect son: polite, top of the country in exams and well liked. Almost nobody sees what he thinks underneath.
After his first two test kills shake him, he quickly talks himself into believing that wiping out criminals will make the world better, and that he alone should decide who dies.
When the FBI agent Raye Penber starts tailing him, Light designs a bus-hijacking scheme to learn the agent's name and then kills him without hesitation.
Knowing cameras may be watching, he hides a scrap of the notebook and a tiny TV in a bag of potato chips so he can keep killing while appearing to study.
When L dares Kira on live TV, Light kills the man on screen in a rage, giving away where he lives. Losing to anyone is something he cannot stand.

light-yagami.backstory: Light grew up in a comfortable Tokyo household as the elder child of Soichiro Yagami, a senior officer in the National Police Agency, and his wife Sachiko, with a cheerful younger sister, Sayu. Clever, handsome and praised by every adult around him, he coasted through school at the very top of the national rankings and developed a quiet arrogance along the way. Inherited from his father was a strong sense of justice, which in Light curdled into contempt for a world he saw as rotten and full of criminals who escaped punishment. By his final year of high school he was simply bored. Then the Shinigami Ryuk, bored himself, dropped his Death Note into the human world, and Light found it lying in his schoolyard. He tried it on a couple of criminals just to see, was horrified when it worked, and then decided to use it anyway.

journey.summary: Light begins killing criminals worldwide by writing their names, and the public names the unseen killer Kira. He meets Ryuk and settles on his goal of becoming the god of a crime-free new world.

He kills FBI agents and Naomi Misora to protect himself, then finds L sitting beside him at To-Oh University. The two play an extended game of bluff, each trying to unmask the other while working on the same case.

journey.stage: Misa and the Yotsuba case (Part I)
journey.summary: The Second Kira, Misa Amane, nearly exposes him. Light gives up ownership of the notebook and with it every memory of being Kira, briefly becoming a decent, sincere investigator before he regains them.
With his memories back, he manipulates the Shinigami Rem into killing L to protect Misa. Light then takes over the role of L and leads the task force himself.
Four years later Kira is worshipped worldwide. L's successors close in from two sides, and Light relies on the zealous prosecutor Teru Mikami to carry out killings for him.

Near proves Light is Kira, Matsuda shoots him, and Ryuk, as promised from the start, puts Light's name in his own notebook. In the manga Light dies at the warehouse (chapter 107); in the anime he flees and dies alone on a staircase (episode 37).

lessons.lesson: Power reveals what was already there.
lessons.why: The notebook doesn't change Light so much as give his arrogance a weapon. Within weeks he is killing innocent investigators to protect himself.

lessons.lesson: A just goal can't excuse any method.
lessons.why: Light says he is building a kinder world, but the list of people he kills to get there grows to include agents, allies and anyone in his way.

lessons.lesson: Nobody is above being caught.
lessons.why: His meticulous planning holds for years, yet one overconfident assumption about Mikami's notebook is what finally exposes him at the warehouse.

lessons.lesson: Who you are without power matters.
lessons.why: During his memory loss Light is honest and caring. Those episodes make the person he chose to become as Kira even harder to watch.

qualities.detail: Scolded by Makima for killing a devil another hunter was already fighting, she instantly claims Denji told her to do it. Blaming someone else is her first reflex.
She introduces herself to Denji by telling him to grovel, and on patrol she brags that devils are hiding because they fear her.
Her cat Meowy is the one creature she cares about at first, so much that she is willing to hand Denji over to the Bat Devil to get it back.
She leaps into fights swinging huge hammers made from her own blood and laughs while soaked in it.
Moved into Aki's apartment, she refuses to bathe, won't flush the toilet and dumps her vegetables on Denji's plate.

chainsaw-man-power.backstory: Power is a Fiend: the Blood Devil inhabiting a human corpse rather than a human who made a deal with one. The series says little about her life before Public Safety beyond what she brags about, which is that she was once a fearsome devil. What it does show is Meowy, a stray cat she originally took in planning to fatten it up and eat it, and ended up loving instead. When the Bat Devil seized Meowy, Power was desperate to get her back, and that search for the cat is tangled up with her first mission alongside Denji. By the time she enters the story she works as a devil hunter for Makima's Special Division 4, a hard-to-control asset kept on a short leash, and she is assigned to patrol with Denji.

journey.summary: She tricks Denji into helping get Meowy back, then tries to hand him to the Bat Devil. Denji saves both her and the cat anyway, and their bickering partnership begins.

journey.stage: Life with Aki and Denji (anime season 1)
journey.summary: Makima moves her into Aki's apartment, where she is an awful but oddly lovable housemate. Through the Eternity Devil trap and the Katana Man fights, she becomes a real member of the team.
Dragged into Hell with the others, she meets the Darkness Devil and comes back badly traumatised. Denji and Aki look after her, and she starts to see them as her first true friends.
She is shattered when Aki becomes the Gun Fiend and dies. Soon after, Makima shoots and kills her in front of Denji (manga chapter 81).
Her blood inside Denji lets her return briefly as the Blood Devil and pull him out of despair. Before fading she makes him promise to find her reborn self in Hell and make her Power again.
After Pochita erases himself, the story restarts: Power saves Denji from the yakuza with her blood, and the two are recruited into Public Safety by Nayuta.

lessons.lesson: People can grow past their worst instincts.
lessons.why: Power starts by trying to sacrifice Denji for her cat. By the end of Part 1 she gives her life to save him instead.

lessons.lesson: Fear is easier to carry with company.
lessons.why: After the Darkness Devil, she can't be alone. Denji and Aki helping her through it is one of the gentlest stretches of the series.

lessons.lesson: Friendship doesn't have to look tidy.
lessons.why: She lies, steals food and shouts constantly, yet her bond with Denji is the most honest one in his life.

lessons.lesson: Some promises outlast death.
lessons.why: Her parting request to Denji, to find her and make her Power again, becomes a thread the story keeps returning to all the way to its final pages.

qualities.detail: Any comment, real or imagined, about his height sets him off instantly. Under the running joke is a teenager who hates being underestimated.
He burned down his own family home before setting out, so there would be nothing to retreat to until he and Al had their bodies back.
He can transmute just by clapping his hands, and he uses it creatively, building weapons and escape routes from whatever is around him mid-fight.
In Liore he exposes the false priest Cornello, and the horror of what Shou Tucker did to his daughter Nina haunts him long afterwards. He takes other people's suffering personally.
Even as a military 'human weapon', Ed refuses to take a life, a line he holds even when enemies are trying to kill him.

edward-elric.backstory: Edward grew up in the farming village of Resembool alongside Alphonse, his younger brother, and their mother, Trisha. Their father, the alchemist Van Hohenheim, left when the boys were small, and they taught themselves alchemy from his books. When Trisha died of illness, the brothers spent years studying in secret, including training under the alchemist Izumi Curtis, and then tried to bring her back through human transmutation, alchemy's greatest taboo. It failed horribly. Ed lost his left leg at the Gate of Truth and Al lost his entire body, so Ed gave his right arm to bind his brother's soul to a suit of armour. Their neighbours Pinako and Winry Rockbell fitted Ed with automail limbs, and at twelve he became the youngest State Alchemist ever, taking the title Fullmetal Alchemist. Before leaving, the brothers burned their house down so they could not turn back.

journey.stage: Liore and the Freezing Alchemist (Brotherhood ep. 1-3)
journey.summary: Already a famous State Alchemist, Ed hunts for the Philosopher's Stone and exposes the cult leader Cornello in Liore, whose 'miracles' come from a fake stone.
Shou Tucker's crime against his own daughter shakes Ed's faith in alchemy. Soon after, Scar, an Ishvalan killing State Alchemists, smashes Ed's automail arm and nearly kills both brothers.
Researching the Stone in Central, the brothers discover it is made from human lives and run into the homunculi. Their friend Maes Hughes is murdered for getting too close to the truth.

Ed teams up with the Xingese prince Ling Yao, gets swallowed by Gluttony and escapes, and learns that the being called Father runs the country. He heads north to Briggs, where Kimblee uses Winry as leverage to force his cooperation.

Alongside Mustang, Scar, Hohenheim and many others, he fights Father in Central. In the final battle (manga chapter 108; Brotherhood ep. 63) he trades his own Gate, and with it his alchemy, to bring Al's body back.
Two years later he leaves to study in the west, awkwardly proposing to Winry using the language of equivalent exchange. The final photo shows them married with two children.

lessons.lesson: Some losses can't be undone, only carried.
lessons.why: The brothers' attempt to revive their mother costs them their bodies. The whole series is Ed learning to live with that mistake instead of erasing it.

lessons.lesson: Every gain has a price.
lessons.why: Ed's world runs on equivalent exchange. At the end he pays for Al's body with his alchemy, and finds that the trade was worth it.

lessons.lesson: Refusing to kill is a real stance, not a weakness.
lessons.why: Others call him naive for it, but he keeps to it through the entire war with Father.

lessons.lesson: Let others share the weight.
lessons.why: Ed starts out trying to fix everything with Al alone. He wins on the Promised Day only because so many allies fight beside him.

qualities.detail: By the time Kariya sees her again in Fate/Zero, the Matou family's cruel 'training' has left her quiet, empty and resigned to her fate. That flat calm horrifies him more than tears would.
In Fate/stay night she comes to Shirou's house almost every day to help with cooking and chores, never asking for much in return.
Her crush on Shirou is obvious to everyone but Shirou. She shows it through small, steady acts of care rather than words.
She has real magical talent but no wish to take part in the Holy Grail War, and in Heaven's Feel she is revealed to have handed command of her Servant to Shinji rather than fight.

sakura-matou.backstory: Sakura was born Sakura Tohsaka, the younger daughter of the mage Tokiomi Tohsaka and his wife Aoi, and the little sister of Rin. Both girls showed unusual magical potential, but a mage family passes its craft to only one heir. When the ancient mage Zouken Matou, whose heir Shinji had no aptitude for magecraft, offered to adopt Sakura as the Matou successor, Tokiomi agreed, believing it would give her a future. Instead, Zouken subjected the child to cruel conditioning with crest worms to force her body to fit the Matou magecraft. By the time Fate/Zero begins, she has become withdrawn and emotionally empty. Kariya Matou, Zouken's son and Aoi's childhood friend, discovers what the Matous have done to her and strikes a bargain with his father: if he claims the Grail in the Fourth Holy Grail War, the girl goes free and returns home.

journey.summary: Kariya visits the Tohsakas, learns Sakura has been given to the Matous and is horrified by what he finds. He lets Zouken implant worms in his own body to gain enough magic to enter the war for her sake.
Kariya fights as Berserker's Master, wrecking his body in the process, but he fails. Sakura stays trapped in the Matou house, and after the war Zouken implants a fragment of the Grail inside her.

journey.stage: Fate and Unlimited Blade Works routes (Fate/stay night)
journey.summary: Ten years later she is a first-year high schooler and Shinji's sister, a familiar presence in Shirou's kitchen. In these routes she stays on the edge of the main story.

journey.stage: Heaven's Feel route (Fate/stay night; Ufotable film trilogy)
journey.summary: She is revealed as Rider's true Master, who passed command to Shinji, and as a mage of the rare Imaginary Numbers attribute. The Grail fragment lets the Shadow act through her at night, and Zouken and Kirei's schemes push her into becoming the vengeful Dark Sakura.

Rin faces her intending to kill her but can't do it, and tells Sakura she never stopped caring. Sakura holds on to herself just long enough that Shirou can pull her free of the Shadow; in the True End she lives on with Shirou and Rider.
In the follow-up she is more confident: captain of the archery club, head of the Matou household and on far closer terms with Rin.

lessons.lesson: Silence isn't the same as being fine.
lessons.why: Sakura's calm in Fate/Zero is a survival habit, not peace. Heaven's Feel shows how much pain and anger was hidden under it.

lessons.lesson: One person's care can be a lifeline.
lessons.why: Her daily visits to Shirou's home are the one normal thing she has. Being chosen and protected by him is what eventually helps pull her back.

lessons.lesson: Family bonds can survive long distance.
lessons.why: Years of separation leave her resenting Rin, yet their confrontation ends with Rin refusing to kill her, and the two sisters reconnecting.

lessons.lesson: Healing can look ordinary.
lessons.why: In hollow ataraxia, recovery means running a club, managing a household and cooking with her sister. Small, everyday steps are the victory.

qualities.detail: Against the vampire Straizo he opens with a Tommy gun, then sneaks a grenade onto his opponent. Joseph prefers dirty tricks and surprises to fair fights.
His signature move is telling enemies exactly what they're about to say. Getting inside their heads is half of how he wins.
He shows little respect for police, gangsters or anyone in charge, though he softens instantly for his grandmother Erina.
When he hears that Speedwagon, whom he sees as an uncle, has been attacked, he goes after Straizo without stopping to think.
His 'secret technique' is running away. It looks cowardly, but he uses it to buy time and lure enemies into a better spot, as he does with Wamuu.

joseph-joestar.backstory: Joseph was born in England to George Joestar II, son of Jonathan and Erina, and a woman named Elizabeth, a Hamon user raised by the master Straizo. Joseph was still an infant when a zombie disguised as a respected British air-corps officer killed George. Elizabeth destroyed the creature, yet because of who it appeared to be, she was treated as a murderer, and the Speedwagon Foundation gave her a new identity and she went into hiding in Venice as Lisa Lisa. Erina raised Joseph alone and kept the family's dark history from him so he would not suffer the same fate as his father and grandfather. Joseph grew up brash, clever and fond of trouble, with an untrained natural talent for Hamon. In 1938 he and Erina relocate across the Atlantic to New York, where the story of Battle Tendency opens.

journey.stage: New York and Straizo (Battle Tendency, anime ep. 10-11)
journey.summary: After befriending Smokey Brown, a boy who tried to rob him, Joseph learns that Straizo has betrayed Speedwagon and turned himself into a vampire. He defeats Straizo and hears that a Pillar Man is about to wake.

He rescues Speedwagon from the Pillar Man Santana and tricks it into turning to stone. In Rome he meets Caesar Zeppeli, but Wamuu, Esidisi and Kars awaken, and Joseph ends up with poison rings in his body and 33 days to win the antidotes.
On an island near Venice he and Caesar train under the stern Lisa Lisa. Joseph defeats Esidisi, then loses Caesar, who dies fighting Wamuu but sends Joseph the antidote.

journey.stage: Swiss Alps and Kars (Battle Tendency finale)
journey.summary: Joseph defeats Wamuu in a chariot duel, and Lisa Lisa is revealed to be his long-lost mother. Kars becomes the Ultimate Being, but a volcanic eruption launches him into space; Joseph loses his left hand, and Suzi Q nurses him back to health and later marries him.

Fifty years later he has the Stand Hermit Purple and travels to Egypt with Jotaro and allies to save his daughter Holly. DIO kills him by draining his blood, but Jotaro revives him with a transfusion from DIO's body.
Now elderly and frail, he travels to Morioh and meets Josuke Higashikata, the son he fathered outside his marriage.

lessons.lesson: Cleverness can beat raw strength.
lessons.why: Joseph is outmatched by every Pillar Man, yet he wins with traps, bluffs and improvised weapons rather than power.

lessons.lesson: Retreat is fine if it serves a plan.
lessons.why: His running away is a running joke, but against Wamuu it turns a losing fight into a winning one.

lessons.lesson: Grief can sharpen resolve.
lessons.why: Losing Caesar breaks him for a moment, then pushes him into his most serious fights of the series.

lessons.lesson: Showing up for family matters most.
lessons.why: Fifty years later the brash kid from New York is the one who gathers a team and crosses the world to save his daughter.

qualities.detail: He threatens Izuku not to even apply to U.A., wanting to be the only student from their school to get in. Being first is part of how he sees himself.
When he wins the Sports Festival but feels his opponent didn't give everything, he refuses to accept the result. A hollow win means nothing to him.
His Explosion Quirk is powerful, but what sets him apart is how fast he reads a fight and adapts mid-battle, using blasts for both attack and movement.
When a younger Izuku offered him a hand when Katsuki slipped into a river, Katsuki took it as an insult. He would rather struggle than be looked down on.
After Izuku outthinks him in the first-year battle trial and he sees Shoto's power, his confidence cracks and he is shaken to the point of tears.

katsuki-bakugou.backstory: Katsuki grew up in the same neighbourhood as Izuku Midoriya, the son of Mitsuki and Masaru Bakugo. His Explosion Quirk, which lets him ignite sweat from his palms, appeared early, and constant praise from adults convinced him he was destined to be the greatest hero, just like their shared idol All Might. Izuku turned out to be Quirkless, and Katsuki's attitude towards his old friend soured into contempt. He nicknamed him 'Deku', a word suggesting someone useless, and bullied him for years. Much later Katsuki admits the real reason: Izuku's stubborn, selfless instinct to help people made Katsuki feel inferior, and he took that out on him. By their last year at Aldera Junior High he is top of his class, aggressive, worshipped by his followers and sure of his path to U.A.

journey.summary: Captured by the Sludge Villain, he is shocked when Quirkless Izuku runs in to try to save him. Both get into U.A.'s Class 1-A, and losing the battle trial to Izuku hits him hard.

journey.stage: Sports Festival and Forest Training Camp (Seasons 2-3)
journey.summary: He takes first place at the Sports Festival but rejects the win as hollow. During the summer camp the League of Villains kidnaps him and tries to recruit him, and he flatly refuses.

All Might rescues him but uses the last of his power against All For One, and Katsuki blames himself for ending his idol's career. After failing the provisional license exam, he works out Izuku's secret and challenges him to a fight, after which All Might explains One For All's history to him.

Training alongside Izuku and Shoto under Endeavor, he grows into a teammate and starts helping Izuku master his growing powers. In the battle against the Paranormal Liberation Front, he throws himself in front of a strike meant for Izuku.
When Izuku goes off alone, Katsuki helps Class 1-A bring him back and finally apologises, admitting he bullied Izuku out of jealousy and an inferiority complex.
Shigaraki, possessed by All For One, ruptures his heart and he briefly dies. Edgeshot restarts it, and Katsuki rejoins the fight, helping clear the way for Izuku's final punch.
After graduating he ranks among Japan's leading pro heroes and helps lead the funding for a powered suit that lets Izuku become a hero again.

lessons.lesson: Insecurity often wears the mask of arrogance.
lessons.why: Katsuki's bullying was never about Izuku's weakness. He admits it came from feeling small next to someone with a hero's heart.

lessons.lesson: A real apology names what you did.
lessons.why: His apology to Izuku doesn't excuse anything; he spells out what he did and why it was wrong. That honesty is what changes their relationship.

lessons.lesson: Winning means more when others are with you.
lessons.why: He starts as a lone fighter who refuses help and ends up shielding Izuku and fighting as part of a team in the Final War.

lessons.lesson: Guilt is better faced than buried.
lessons.why: His guilt over All Might having to retire nearly derails him. Saying it out loud in his fight with Izuku is what lets him move forward.

qualities.detail: He makes his entrance floating down a river and greets the boy who pulls him out with jokes. Humour is how he keeps everyone, including himself, at a distance.
While supposedly hunting a man-eating tiger with Atsushi, he quietly works out that Atsushi himself is the tiger, and sets up the night around proving it.
He spots Atsushi's potential right away and brings him into the Armed Detective Agency, later telling his old protégé Akutagawa that the new recruit is the better student.
He lets the Port Mafia capture him and chain him up, treating the cell as a place to gather information rather than as a defeat.
Coworkers see him dodge paperwork and annoy his partner Kunikida, yet he is usually several steps ahead of everyone in the room.

osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.backstory: Before the Armed Detective Agency, Dazai belonged to Yokohama's Port Mafia. He joined as a teenager under its boss, Ogai Mori, and partnered with Chuuya Nakahara; the pair became so feared that the underworld called them Double Black. Dazai rose to be the youngest executive in the Mafia's history and was a brilliant, cold strategist. His closest friends there were the low-ranking member Oda Sakunosuke, who refused to kill, and the government informant Ango Sakaguchi. Oda died in a conflict with the group Mimic that Mori had quietly engineered for the Mafia's benefit. His dying words urged Dazai to choose the side that rescues others. Dazai walked away from the Mafia and spent about two years laying low while Ango helped scrub his record, then joined the Agency at twenty under Fukuzawa, paired with Doppo Kunikida.

journey.summary: He recruits Atsushi into the Agency and steers him through his first clashes with the Port Mafia. He allows himself to be captured and taunts Akutagawa, his former subordinate, from his cell.
The story flashes back to his Mafia days with Oda and Ango, ending with Oda's death and Dazai's decision to leave.

When the American organisation known as the Guild attacks Yokohama, Dazai helps broker a temporary truce that puts the Agency and the Port Mafia on the same side and briefly reunites with Chuuya as Double Black.

Fyodor Dostoyevsky, leader of the Rats in the House of the Dead, pits the Agency and the Port Mafia against one another. Dazai is shot and hospitalised, then tracks Fyodor down with help from the Guild and has him arrested.

Framed and hunted by the government's Hunting Dogs, the Agency scatters, and Dazai ends up in the European prison Meursault alongside Fyodor. He escapes with Sigma's help as part of a plan with Ango, then is shot by a seemingly turned Chuuya.
The anime reveals that Chuuya only pretended to be a vampire and faked Dazai's death while the plan to stop Fyodor played out. The manga continues as of November 2026, with Dazai alive.

lessons.lesson: One friend's words can redirect a life.
lessons.why: Oda's last request is the reason Dazai leaves the Mafia. Everything he does at the Agency is an attempt to honour it.

lessons.lesson: People can change sides for good.
lessons.why: Once the Mafia's youngest executive, he now uses the same intellect to protect Yokohama. The story keeps testing whether that change is real.

lessons.lesson: Believing in someone can help them believe in themselves.
lessons.why: Dazai backs Atsushi when the boy thinks he's worthless. That faith helps turn a hungry orphan into a capable agent.

lessons.lesson: Humour isn't the same as being okay.
lessons.why: His jokes about death mask real darkness in his past. The series lets you laugh with him while showing that the pain under it is serious.

qualities.detail: Dropped into a fantasy kingdom in his tracksuit, he strikes poses and talks like the hero of a game. The swagger covers how little he can actually do.
He throws himself into Emilia's search for her stolen insignia within minutes of meeting her, with no plan and no fighting ability.
Each time Return by Death resets him, he goes back in and tries again to save the people he has just watched die, even when it breaks him.
A force connected to the Witch of Envy stops him whenever he tries to explain his loops, so he carries every death alone while others grow suspicious of him.
Without magic or swordsmanship, he relies on stamina from his daily workouts, quick reflexes and whatever he learned in earlier loops.

subaru-natsuki.backstory: Subaru Natsuki was an ordinary Japanese teenager who had drifted into a shut-in life. Growing up, he wanted to be like his father, a popular and respected man in their community, and for a while he played the energetic kid who could do anything. As he got older he realised he couldn't live up to that image, and the gap ate at him until he stopped going to school and stayed home. The Sanctuary trials later show that his parents, especially his mother, never stopped caring, and that he had never actually told them how he felt. Despite being a hikikomori he kept exercising every day with basic bodyweight drills. One night, walking home from a convenience store with snacks in hand, he was suddenly pulled into the Kingdom of Lugunica, where he would discover his only power: dying and coming back.

journey.summary: He meets Emilia and dies alongside her at the hands of the assassin Elsa, discovering Return by Death. After failed loops he finally calls for help, and the knight Reinhard arrives to save them.
Working as a servant, he keeps dying to a curse and to Rem, who suspects him. He learns to see the household as real people and wins Rem's trust by saving the village from cursed beasts.

journey.stage: Arc 3: Royal Selection and the White Whale (Season 1)
journey.summary: His need for validation leads him to humiliate himself and Emilia at the Royal Selection. After many failed loops he breaks down to Rem, who calls him her hero; he then builds an alliance that kills the White Whale and defeats the Sin Archbishop Petelgeuse, though Rem is left in a coma.

Facing trials about his past and his habit of treating his own life as worthless, he learns to rely on his friends. He saves both the Sanctuary and the mansion, persuades Beatrice to live as his contracted spirit and is knighted by Emilia.
A year later the Witch Cult attacks the water city of Priestella. Subaru rallies the citizens with a speech and works out how to break Regulus's invulnerability.
Seeking a cure for the Cult's victims at a remote tower, Subaru suddenly loses every memory of his life in Lugunica and has to work out who he has become.

lessons.lesson: Asking for help is a strength.
lessons.why: Subaru's very first win comes when he stops trying to be the hero and simply yells for help. The lesson keeps coming back each arc.

lessons.lesson: Admitting your flaws can be the turning point.
lessons.why: He only breaks out of his worst loops in Arc 3 after confessing to Rem how small and useless he feels. Her answer gives him something to stand on.

lessons.lesson: Your own life counts too.
lessons.why: In the Sanctuary he treats dying as a tool and is confronted with how much his deaths hurt others. Learning to value himself is a big part of his growth.

lessons.lesson: Respect people as people, not plot devices.
lessons.why: Early on he acts like the star of a fantasy game. He makes progress only when he starts treating Rem, Ram and the others as people with their own reasons.

qualities.detail: He scores exactly 50 points on every subject of the entrance exam. It's a perfect way to stay invisible, and it makes his teacher and the student council president suspicious.
Before the first midterm he quietly buys an old test from an upperclassman with private points, reading the school's rules as a toolkit rather than a limit.
When Sudo is at risk of expulsion over a fight, Kiyotaka works the problem from the shadows and lets Suzune and others take the visible role.
His self-introduction on day one is so clumsy that Suzune openly mocks it. Making ordinary friends is genuinely hard for him.
His inner narration treats classmates as pieces to be used. He tells himself that winning matters more than how people feel about it.

kiyotaka-ayanokouji.backstory: Kiyotaka is the son of a powerful man who runs a secret facility called the White Room, where children were put through relentless tests and training designed to produce people with near-superhuman abilities. Kiyotaka was raised there and was the only one to meet every one of its standards. He grew up with little ordinary human contact, and his father's lessons shaped his view that other people are tools for reaching a goal. Wanting a taste of freedom, he enrolled at the Advanced Nurturing High School, a government-run school cut off from the outside world, where his father cannot easily reach him. He deliberately hid his abilities on the entrance exam, scoring exactly half marks in every subject, and landed in Class D, the lowest-ranked class. His father later tries to pressure the school into expelling him, which tells Kiyotaka that his escape is far from secure.

journey.summary: Class D blows its monthly points and learns that classes rise and fall by merit. Kiyotaka helps keep the weakest students from expulsion, including spending points to save Sudo after a failed test.

journey.stage: Sudo's case and the island exam (Season 1)
journey.summary: He uncovers a witness, Airi Sakura, to clear Sudo of a staged assault, then wins the week-long survival exam on an uninhabited island for Class D through a plan nobody else sees until the results. He also learns that his father has asked the school to expel him.

journey.stage: Cruise ship, Sports Festival and Ryuen (Season 2)
journey.summary: As exams grow more complex, Class C's leader Kakeru Ryuen hunts for the hidden strategist in Class D. When Ryuen corners Kei Karuizawa on the school rooftop, Kiyotaka confronts him in person and beats him and his group, and Ryuen steps down as his class's leader. Around the same time his father visits the school and offers to take him out; Kiyotaka refuses.

An acting director named Tsukishiro arrives and starts manipulating special exams to get Kiyotaka expelled. Kiyotaka keeps steering Class D from the background through the year's final exams, and by the start of second year he and Kei are secretly dating.

journey.stage: Second year (light novels; anime from Season 4)
journey.summary: A White Room student is planted among the new first-years and a bounty is placed on his expulsion, while Tsukishiro keeps up the pressure. The light novels are ongoing, Season 4 aired in April-June 2026, with a fifth season on the way.

lessons.lesson: Rules reward people who read them closely.
lessons.why: Kiyotaka's early wins come from understanding the school's point system better than everyone else, like buying an old test that was never forbidden.

lessons.lesson: Treating people as tools has a cost.
lessons.why: The series lets you admire his plans while showing how coldly he uses classmates, and whether he can change is one of its big questions.

lessons.lesson: Credit isn't the same as impact.
lessons.why: He lets Suzune and others take the spotlight for victories he planned. The show treats influence as something that can stay invisible.

lessons.lesson: Freedom has to be defended.
lessons.why: He enrolled to get away from the White Room, and his father's attempts to pull him back turn that freedom into something he has to fight for.

qualities.detail: When the starving pirate Gin is thrown out of the Baratie with no money, Sanji quietly brings him a hot meal anyway. Nobody who is truly hungry gets turned away by him.
He fights only with kicks, keeping his hands safe for the kitchen. Being a cook comes before being a fighter.
He swoons over every woman he meets and refuses to hurt one, a rule he keeps even when it nearly gets him killed.
While waiting tables he openly snubs the Marine lieutenant Fullbody, and when the officer wastes the food served to him, Sanji beats him up. Throwing away a meal is the one thing he won't tolerate.
He owes Zeff his life and stubbornly refuses to leave the Baratie, even as it's attacked. When he finally sails off, he drops to his knees in tears to thank the old man.

sanji.backstory: Sanji was born a prince of the Germa Kingdom, a floating nation run by his father, Vinsmoke Judge, who experimented on his children to make them stronger and emotionless. Their mother Sora secretly took a drug to undo the changes, and only Sanji was affected: he grew up with ordinary strength and real feelings. Judge called him a failure and locked him away while his brothers bullied him, until his sister Reiju helped him escape, and Judge ordered him never to reveal he was a Vinsmoke. Working as a young kitchen hand on a passenger ship, he was swept overboard when the pirate 'Red Foot' Zeff attacked. Stranded together on a rock, Zeff gave the boy all their food. After their rescue, the pair built the floating restaurant Baratie, where Zeff trained Sanji as a cook and in kick-based fighting. Both dreamed of finding the All Blue.

journey.summary: He meets Luffy, defends the restaurant from Don Krieg's pirates and finally accepts that he can leave Zeff to chase his own dream. He joins the Straw Hats as their cook.
He fights Fish-Men to free Nami's village, then, in Arabasta, poses as 'Mr. Prince' to lure Crocodile away and help the crew escape a trap.
He tracks Robin onto the sea train to the judicial island, refuses to strike the CP9 agent Kalifa because she is a woman, and beats Jabra with his new Diable Jambe.
He offers his own life to Bartholomew Kuma in exchange for Luffy's. During the two-year separation he trains in the Kamabakka Kingdom and learns Sky Walk.

Forced into a political marriage with Big Mom's daughter Pudding, he leaves the crew to protect them and even fights Luffy to push him away. In the end he admits he wants to come back and helps save both the crew and his family.
In Wano he destroys his family's Raid Suit rather than become like his brothers, then defeats Queen. On Egghead he protects Nami and Bonney from powerful foes as the crew faces the Navy.

lessons.lesson: Hunger isn't something to punish.
lessons.why: Sanji feeds Gin, an enemy pirate, because he remembers starving on a rock with Zeff. Kindness learned in hard times gets passed on.

lessons.lesson: Gratitude can hold you back if you never let yourself go.
lessons.why: Sanji nearly stays at the Baratie forever out of debt to Zeff. Leaving with Luffy is how he honours their shared dream.

lessons.lesson: Your worth isn't what your family says it is.
lessons.why: Judge called him a failure, but the qualities his father hated, his compassion and his feelings, are what make Sanji a hero.

lessons.lesson: It's okay to ask for help.
lessons.why: On Whole Cake Island he tries to handle everything alone. Only when he admits to Luffy that he wants to stay with the crew can his friends help him save everyone.
